subject: Infra pathways & controls - HIPAA / SOC2 follow-up and evidence asks
content:
Message 1 (2027-04-28T15:12:00-07:00)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@healthops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Infra pathways & controls - HIPAA / SOC2 follow-up and evidence asks

Hi Tim — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist.

High-level assessment (from our discovery):
- Primary requirement: HIPAA PHI processing in production, BAA required.
- Audit needs: SOC2 Type II attestation or equivalent evidence for controls; detailed network diagrams and change logs for onboarding/audit.
- Preference/tight constraints: HealthOps prefers not to host PHI outside US and wants proof of encryption-in-transit and at-rest with customer KMS/HSM support.

Hosting options we discussed (short form):
1) Hosted API (fastest)
   - Pros: immediate start, managed runtime, built-in multi-tenant controls;
   - Cons: requires Redwood-signed BAA + SOC2 evidence and a documented isolation/segregation plan.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools)
   - Pros: stronger logical separation, predictable throughput; can be coupled with a VPC peering boundary for tighter network controls.
   - Cons: longer provisioning lead time, higher committed cost.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem)
   - Pros: full network isolation, customer-managed infra, best for strict audit/regulation;
   - Cons: integration effort, on-prem ops or private control plane.

Specific evidence you asked for on the call — we attached a short summary (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_summary.pdf) and a living checklist (summary-of-evidence-required.xlsx):
- SOC2 Type II report (summary + cover letter)
- Current SOC2 scope (services in scope / excluded)
- Encryption/encryption key management notes (KMS/HSM integration options)
- Network diagram showing host routing, load balancers, firewall ACLs, peering/VPN details
- Data retention & deletion policy, and secure-delete proof points
- BAAs: a draft BAA (we can provide a template and iterate)

Proposed next steps / owners / target dates:
- Redwood to deliver: SOC2 attestation summary + network diagram (owner: Ben Carter) — target: 2027-05-03
- Redwood to circulate: draft BAA for HealthOps review (owner: Marissa Cole) — target: 2027-05-04
- Schedule 30-45m tech deep-dive with your infra/security team to align on routing and egress (owner: Lauren) — proposed slot: 2027-05-05 10:00 PT
- HealthOps to share: internal control checklist and any mandatory contractual clauses (owner: Tim) — please attach in reply

If it helps, Ben can sketch a recommended default: start on Hosted API behind a BAA while we prepare a Dedicated-capacity plan you can transition to (if required) — that minimizes time-to-value while giving you the option to harden isolation later.

Thanks — I’ve attached the two files I referenced. Let me know if the dates look achievable and whether you want Ben or Vivek to join the deep-dive for technical mapping.

—
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_summary.pdf (stub), summary-of-evidence-required.xlsx (stub)

Message 3 (2027-04-30T08:43:00-07:00)
From: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@healthops.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Infra pathways & controls - HIPAA / SOC2 follow-up and evidence asks

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) BAA + Hosted API: is Redwood able to sign a BAA for Hosted API customers that process PHI? If so, are there any feature restrictions (e.g., certain integrations disabled)?
2) SOC2: we need the Type II report and a control mapping. Will the summary include the date range of the audit and the auditor firm?
3) Keys: we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key). Is that supported in Hosted API mode or only for Dedicated/Private?
4) Data residency: can you confirm the US-only hosting option and whether backups are geo-redundant inside the US only?
5) Audit window: our auditors may ask to run a 2-week control validation. Will Redwood support evidence collection for such a window (logs, config snapshots)?
6) Cost: high-level delta for Dedicated vs Private (per month) is helpful so we can budget.

I’m attaching our internal requirements doc for reference (healthops_internal-requirements.pdf). If you can answer the Qs above in the deep-dive that will put us in a good position to move forward.

Best,
Tim Jensen
Head of Security & Compliance
HealthOps
tim.jensen@healthops.com | +1 (503) 555-0199

Attachments: healthops_internal-requirements.pdf (external)

Message 4 (2027-05-01T09:21:00-07:00)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@healthops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Infra pathways & controls - HIPAA / SOC2 follow-up and evidence asks

Tim — thanks for the questions and for the document. Short answers here and we’ll cover details in the tech deep-dive:

1) BAA + Hosted API: Yes — Redwood will sign a BAA for Hosted API customers that need PHI processing. There are no feature-level restrictions by default; certain third-party integrations can be disabled per-account if requested. (Owner: Marissa)
2) SOC2: We will provide the Type II report summary with audit period and auditor firm noted (Ben will attach the redacted report).
3) Keys: Customer-managed keys are supported in Dedicated and Private today. For Hosted API we offer a customer-key option via KMS envelopes for some plans; I’ll have Vivek confirm supported modes and any limitations.
4) Data residency: we support US-only hosting on the Redwood US zone; backups can be restricted to US-only regions.
5) Audit window: we can provide logs, config snapshots, and run tailored evidence exports for a 2-week validation window. We’ll need a short runbook from your auditors on what they want to verify.
6) Cost: Ben will follow up with a short delta estimate for Dedicated vs Private (ballpark monthly).

Next steps / owners (condensed):
- Ben: SOC2 pack + auditor + mapping — due 2027-05-03 (deliver via Drive link)
- Marissa: BAA draft v2 — due 2027-05-04
- Vivek: KMS/keys limitations doc + pen-test summary — due 2027-05-06
- Lauren: schedule tech deep-dive 2027-05-05 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow)

We’ll upload the deliverables to the shared drive and share the folder link in the calendar invite. Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
